With 10+ years of international experience in data analytics, AI, and business intelligence tool development, I specialize in predictive modeling, big data, data visualization technologies, and generative AI.

My academic journey includes an M.Sc. in Biomedical Engineering from the University of Bologna and a PhD in Bioinformatics from ETH Zurich, providing a strong foundation in complex data analysis and innovative solution development. My mission is to empower clients through AI-driven solutions, solving complex business challenges and driving growth.

headline: Filmmaker: Writer, Director, Producer, Editor
topSkills: Leadership • Marketing • Creative Direction • Clear Vision • Film Production
about:
I am an LA-based filmmaker with twenty years of experience as a creative leader and storyteller. I started my creative journey when I wrote my first feature at 15, adapted/directed a four-act play at 17, and wrote/directed/produced a no budget indie feature at 20. Since then, I have self-funded several award-winning short films, written two television pilots, and completed seven feature-length screenplays.

Throughout my career, I have created impactful global content for both creative and government agencies in Chicago, DC, London, New York, and Los Angeles — bringing ideas to life from concept to delivery. My recent projects include collaborations with Bloomberg, Warner Bros. Discovery, Rolling Stone, Bain & Company, Freddie Mac, Cure., The National Association of Theatre Owners, and the US Department of State — earning millions of views and high-levels of engagement across various sectors of media and entertainment.

My scripts "Throne of Blood" and “The Man Who Left His Wife and Had a Nifty Time” have both been recognized as Second Rounders by the Austin Film Festival. In 2024, my short films "Anyone for President" and “Happy Hour” screened at the TCL Chinese Theatres in Hollywood.

My next feature project is "Venor" and currently seeking partners. The script has recently been acknowledged by Hollywood Horrorfest and was in the top twenty percentile of the Academy Nicholl Fellowship.

IATSE, Local #700 Editor.

publications.title: Mind the Gap - Crafting a Business-Centric IT Skills Strategy
publications.description:
Business leaders routinely invest significant resources to develop and deliver ambitious business plans, taking time and great care to work through the strategic, operational and financial details. But the essential contribution of key people, and hence skills, to the successful implementation of the strategy is often neglected. Consequently, a damaging imbalance emerges between growth targets and the core capabilities required to achieve those goals.

This disconnect has become exacerbated in recent years. As IT becomes a more critical enabler of business today, many IT organizations have failed to adopt a comprehensive human capital strategy. While much focus has been placed on systems, technical capabilities and IT assets, ensuring that the organization has the proper talent in place and is equipped with the right skills to align with and drive the evolving business capabilities of the enterprise has typically taken a back seat.

Although the effects are not always immediately obvious, experience has shown that the inability to predict key skills requirements and ensure that the right talent is in place when and where needed undermines business performance in the long term. The results are missed growth targets, mediocre productivity and higher recruiting costs.

publications.title: How to make your target operating model a reality?
publications.description:
Whether facing the challenges of austerity measures and regulatory changes, an increasingly dynamic and globalized business environment, or the difficulties posed by an ever more complex digital and data-driven market, defining the right target operating model is crucial for steering the course to profitable growth. As an overall operations and technology ecosystem, a target operating model serves as a company’s blueprint for achieving its strategic vision.

Realizing the full benefits of a target operating model, however, and regularly adapting it to continually shifting business strategies, can pose significant challenges. No single, ideal target operating model exists. Rather, each company’s model design will depend on its starting point, culture and the optimization goals it has prioritized based on its business strategy, market position and areas of competition, and differentiated client value proposition.

publications.title: The Next Generation EPMO
publications.description:
Today, most organizations are facing two major challenges: business uncertainty and an accelerated pace of change. They face adaptive challenges— global changes in societies, markets, customers, competition and technology—which are forcing them to clarify their values, develop new strategies and learn new ways of operating. In this uncertain environment, companies must execute on an increasingly complex stage. The ability to develop and implement new strategic initiatives and change gears rapidly is becoming a key differentiator and area of competitive advantage.

Yet many companies struggle to successfully execute on these strategic initiatives. The difficulty is blindly attributed to shortcomings in leadership, while, in reality, it is largely associated with ineffective engagement and management. Many senior executives struggle with getting the information they need—when they need it—to make the necessary adjustments and course corrections that are critical to ensuring that large strategic initiatives deliver their target impact.

Kurt Salmon has identified four pillars that shape the framework for the next-generation Enterprise PMO and which will improve the odds of successfully delivering strategic initiatives.

publications.title: Enterprise Integrated Planning: Air Traffic Control for CIOs
publications.description:
For years, companies have been pouring money into resources, processes, and technologies that can help them manage risk.

Risk management involves a judicious mix of preventing the risks that can reasonably be controlled, learning to recognize the ones that can’t be prevented, being prepared to react to minimize damage, and having the resources to recover from the problems that do occur. Technology is an essential component to succeeding in today’s business environment and companies recognize that the complexities of technology require a commitment to the development of more robust capabilities to manage risk and create a more risk-aware culture. Industries with the highest dependency on technology are faced today with the competing requirements of providing a stable, reliable, low cost technology platform for daily business operations (“Run the Business”) and also providing a dynamic, flexible, cost effective capability to modify the technology platform in response to technology or business imperatives (“Change the Business”).

slides.subtitle: review.chicagobooth.edu

slides.title: The Next Frontier of Payment Fraud Prevention
slides.subtitle: Simo Zerrifi on LinkedIn
slides.description: The payments industry has transformed from one of stagnancy to one of radical, sweeping change. New technologies and the rise of digital payments have surfaced in a space that hasn’t made any significant breakthrough in nearly 80 years, particularly in the U.S. There are five mega-trends that are shaping the payments space: Shopping reinvented: The shift to digital platforms for many retailers, the increasing importance of digital commerce, and the related payment experience are forcing merchants to define the best way to accept payments in order to appeal to the widest group of consumers Focus on experience: Consumers are more focused on experiences, which impacts how the actual payment transaction is processed. As customers demand frictionless check-out experiences, businesses need to differentiate in terms of how they engage with their customers to increase conversion rate and satisfaction. Further, as the value of traditional competitive differentiators decreases (e.g., transaction processing speed, convenience, and access), future revenue will need to come from other means; likely more differentiated services or experiences Shifting market frontiers: The rapid development and rise in financial services adoption in Asia/Pacific and Latin American markets leave only MEA, Eastern Europe, and NAM as the greatest opportunities in terms of cash conversion Connected consumers: Technology is more integrated into every action that a consumer takes, creating a new consumer standard. The higher prevalence of exponential technologies—distributed ledger technology (DLT), Internet of Things (IoT) as point-of-sale (POS), wallets, tokenization, and more—will expand consumers’ and merchants’ options for how to pay and receive payment. Personalization: Card rewards for very affluent consumers have reached new levels in recent years. At the same time, more services are being positioned as premium for all consumer segments and the need for personalization is becoming a key competitive advantage Globally, electronic payment volumes continue to grow, and consumers and businesses are conducting more banking activities via online and mobile devices. Convenience is a core feature for consumers and businesses alike, but it must not come at the cost of security. In this fast-changing environment, the ability to detect and prevent payments fraud and financial crime is crucial; cybercrime is a growing threat and the perpetrators have identified payments as a highly profitable target area. Businesses lose approximately 5% of revenue each year due to fraud. In the U.S., card fraud is on the rise both in terms of absolute value lost to fraud and as a share of total card payment value fraud. According to ThreatMetrix Cybercrime report, account takeover attacks have grown 81% year-on-year and 211% for mobile transactions. New account creation attacks are growing 23% and are attacked at a higher rate than the global average at 3.5%. The increased online fraud is driven by the pace of adoption of the EMV standard by merchants as well as the use of other transaction due-diligence tools such as 3D Secure. As a result, issuers are ramping up their emphasis on security as a point of differentiation - recent high-profile data breaches may have card issuers doing more to put security-conscious consumers at ease. Credit score monitoring, card controls, identity theft resources, and ATO protection (e.g. multi-factor authentication, behavioral biometrics) are among the features that issuers are promoting. In Europe, the revised Payment Services Directive (PSD2), which went into effect in January 2018, will have a significant impact on the European payments market. Though the PSD2 regulation is set to revolutionize the banking industry, it also introduces new fraud risks for financial institutions. These risks raise the question once again of how banks, payment providers and merchants can deliver excellent customer experiences without compromising security. In this environment, third-party providers (TPPs) can directly access bank customers’ payments and account information, if permitted to do so by customers. However, this raises questions about data privacy and security; in an increasingly networked ecosystem, identifying attackers will be a challenge. To comply with PSD2’s Strong Customer Authentication (SCA) section, online merchants and financial institutions will need to build additional authentication into their checkout flow while still delivering good user experiences as SCA requires authentication to use at least two of the following three elements: Something the customer knows: password, passphrase, pin, secret fact... Something the customer own: mobile, wearable, smartcard, token, badge... Something the customer is: fingerprint, facial features, voice patterns, DNA signature... Fraud Analytics Platform With malware and Remote Access Tool (RAT) attacks, cybercriminals are able to take over accounts and automate fraud despite traditional fraud detection measures being in place. Using social engineering, fraudsters can gain access to victims’ machines and steal credentials, intercept consumers online, or monitor and intercept consumer activity. Typical fraud detection solutions, such as device recognition, proxy detection, and IP geolocation, are easy for fraudsters to bypass. Digital business requirements are driving IAM and Fraud Prevention to adopt technologies that better establish trust and remove friction. Orthodox user authentication methods based on credentials are still widely used BUT they are not wholly successful across online, mobile and digital channels. Most Command and Control defense strategies lead to customer friction and require an integrated approach to be effective: Orthodox methods add friction and erode UX — Longer, more-complex passwords are harder to remember and type accurately (especially on mobile devices) Orthodox methods can be strong, but brittle — Once credentials or protocols are compromised, there's no resilience Business moments involve fluid, transient relationships — Credential-based methods cannot be used to authenticate total strangers and false positives impair the customer experience Leading banks and merchants began using Machine Learning and Behavioral Biometrics for continuous authentication to prevent real-time fraud and identity theft that occurs as a result of social engineering, Remote Access Trojans, malware or stolen credentials. Some advanced merchants and issuers are moving towards a Progressive Fraud Analytics Platform layered at every stage across the customer journey: Behavioral biometrics work in the background to build up profiles based on a user’s unique actions. How do they type or click? How fast do they move a mouse? Any deviations from the norm alert a merchant or a bank to possible fraudulent activity and allow to stop account takeover attacks in the initial authentication process or when a user has to re-authorize after a 90-day token expires. The software market for advanced fraud detection and prevention solutions has also evolved and is highly fragmented. Buyers (large, medium or small) usually have challenges understanding this segmentation due to the plethora of solutions available in the market as well as the lack of maturity in clearly defining the different use cases that those solutions are solving for. There are many capable point solutions in the market such as NuDetect by NuData Security, Brighterion with its smart agent technology, Biocatch, and ThreatMetrix to name a few; however, buyers are increasingly seeking end-to-end integrated solutions to minimize integration hurdles and complexity in operations. As such, large fraud platform players are partnering with point solution providers to either close gaps and/or increase product capabilities and features (e.g. Kount partnership with BehavioSec). Buyers value the concept of “Fusion” in which platforms’ depth of consortium data, breadth of integration and partner ecosystems drive differentiation. What's next? The commerce experiences of today and tomorrow will continue revolutionizing the payments landscape, making payments the invisible, invaluable part of a customer-first and frictionless experience. Online fraud detection continues to grow in complexity with many solutions measuring dynamic behavioral characteristics. Banks, merchants, and payment vendors should focus on creating a trusted ecosystem and seek orchestrated solutions to improve customer experience. "These thoughts and posts are my own"

slides.title: Now Is The Time to Get Digital Transformations Right
slides.subtitle: Simo Zerrifi on LinkedIn
slides.description: As the digital revolution dramatically reshapes industry after industry, many companies are pursuing large-scale change efforts to capture the benefits of these trends or simply to keep up with competitors. However, organizations are struggling to transform themselves because they are using yesterday’s paradigms to solve today’s problems related to the shift to digital. Many studies have confirmed that organizations that have undertaken such efforts in the past five years have had mixed results, with success in these transformations proving to be elusive. In 2011, GE embarked on an ambitious attempt to digitally transform its product and service offerings. The company created vast digital capabilities, labeling itself a “digital industrial” company, embedding sensors into many products and building a new software platform for the Internet of Things (i.e. Predix). Fast forward to today, investors haven’t acknowledged GE’s digital ambition as the company’s stock price has languished for years and CEO Jeff Immelt was forced to depart the company under pressure from activist investors. The new CEO, John Flannery, has scaled down GE’s digital ambition and is focused primarily on cutting costs. GE is hardly the only company to run into performance issues in the midst of a large digital transformation effort. Lego defunded its Digital Designer virtual building program. Nike halved the size of its digital unit by discontinuing its Nike+ Fuelband activity tracker. Procter & Gamble who aspired to become “the most digital company on the planet” ran into growth challenges in a difficult economy. Burberry set out to be the world’s best digital luxury brand, but performance did not follow. Ford invested heavily in digital initiatives only to see its stock price lag due to cost and quality issues elsewhere in the company. These companies spent millions to develop digital products, infrastructures, and got tremendous media and investor attention, only to encounter significant performance challenges, and often shareholder dissent. What can we learn from these examples of digital dreams conceded? While all these companies had plenty of resources, the big digital bets did not pay off quickly, or abundantly, enough, to counter the drain they represented on the rest of the business. Several factors are intensifying the pressure: investors are valuing top-line revenue growth; rising customer expectations for simple cross-channel experiences are compelling companies to systematically tear down silos, and an organization’s ability to respond to market shifts is becoming a core differentiator. Large-scale transformations are hard, and digital ones are no exception. So, what makes the anatomy of a successful digital transformation? How do you build a successful digital organization? (hint: it isn’t about going paperless) Talking to several leaders about what makes them leaders in their markets points to five key lessons that set successful change efforts apart. These actions suggest ways that other organizations can plan and execute digital transformations successfully: Go big - With blurring lines across industries and services, organizations face many critical choices when considering a response to digital disruptions. They need to address a number of pressing questions: Should they transform their existing business model or build a brand new one? Should they drive down costs to improve the bottom line or focus on customer engagement to drive the top line? Which areas will require most investments to achieve the strategic objectives? Successful organizations manage to get a strong consensus among leaders on the best way forward and favor an all-in, enterprise-wide transformation, rather than constraining the transformation to individual functions or business units or pursuing many different agendas. A more comprehensive scope that targets both the top and bottom lines and engages a substantial share of the workforce increases the chances of creating value-generating opportunities across the organization. Walmart is a great example of a company that decided to take action rather than sit on the sidelines and wait for the inevitable. Despite starting out slow against Amazon, Walmart is increasingly becoming a “digital winner”, as it builds out a fast-growing e-commerce business and also leads in digital innovations when compared to other brick-and-mortar retailers. Walmart focused on improving its mobile app features with the goal of saving consumers time and money, and improving the shopping experience. Walmart has also leveraged technology to improve the in-store customer experience in many ways such as various store pickup options, Scan and Go capability that allows customers to avoid the negative experience of long checkout lines, and strengthening its data and analytics capabilities to capture value, ultimately leading to higher sales and operating efficiencies. Be flexible and adaptive - The fast pace at which digital drives change requires transformations to be adaptive and flexible. Successful organizations are continuously adjusting investment requirements and performance targets as the transformation progresses. Along with the need for adaptable transformation targets, flexible talent allocation is a key differentiator in a digital transformation’s success. Take again the example of Nike. Although it failed in its initial digital transformation efforts, Nike was able to make adjustments to succeed in the future. The company switched its mindset to focus on reinventing its brand and supply chain. Instead of going through middlemen, Nike improved customer engagement through membership opportunities, stronger digital marketing, and powerful data analytics. An end-to-end focus on consumer data allowed Nike to better connect with customers and recommend the right products. It also opened concept stores and improved its online and app experience. The improved digital focus gives Nike a faster product development cycle, which allows it to get new products to market quickly, respond to and set trends and control how many items are produced. At the beginning of 2017, its stock price was $52; it’s now up to nearly $90. Adopt Agile execution approaches and mindsets - The execution of digital transformation initiatives must also be adaptable by adopting agile ways of working and changing the culture to encourage risk-taking, innovation, and collaboration across the organization. The connection between building better software and business agility has been for years a tenuous one at best. But now that Agile is maturing and digital transformation is driving change, companies are now realizing that their best bet for achieving business agility is to take the best of Agile and apply it across the entire organization. Successful organizations create the proper balance between control and autonomy by adopting a ‘holistic’ approach to Agile and implementing it inside and outside IT. However, not every function needs to be organized into agile teams; indeed, such an approach isn’t well suited for some activities. Once a business begins launching dozens or hundreds of agile teams, however, it can’t just leave the other parts of the business alone. Changes are necessary to ensure that the functions that don’t operate as agile teams support the ones that do. Finally, Agile transformation requires a complete rethink of how an organization quantifies and manages risk, as the strategic risks of not being sufficiently agile trump the risks inherent in the Agile transformation itself. BBVA, the leading multinational Spanish bank, reached a landmark milestone in 2019: It transformed the way the Group’s entire 33,000-strong central services division organized itself and worked by incorporating agile methodology techniques into their daily business activities. This change has redefined the traditional concept of departments and functional divisions, establishing a new structure composed of five main blocks for each department: 1) Customer management ("front line"), 2) Project teams, 3) Process teams, 4) Disciplines, and 5) Control. Modernize the core - As digital disruptions impose greater demands on IT systems and organizations, companies must move away from only supporting and working around legacy infrastructure. The need for legacy systems to interact with digital applications is pushing IT to process dramatically increased transaction volumes and operate at speeds greater than the systems were ever designed to handle. Beyond performance challenges, established companies are at a competitive inflection point. New digital disrupters can build a brand-new IT landscape, while companies with legacy systems must seek ways to integrate new, digital technologies harvesting legacy technology to maximize their IT investments. There are many approaches to modernization, such as rehost, replatform and replace. Successful organizations modernize valuable business capabilities through an end-to-end product lifecycle, across all applications, platforms, and ecosystems that comprise the complete capability rather than focusing modernization efforts on a single entity. This approach includes creating flexibility to add new digital layers by redefining the enterprise architecture with microservices at the core. Such a strategy is enabled by the standardization and automation of the IT environment through an open API model, adopting a modern security posture, working in an automated agile operating model, and leveraging new capabilities to drive innovative business solutions. Digital winners are looking to integrate legacy data with analytics engines to break the data silos and unlock value. Capturing the most value from the wealth of potential data begins with excellence in identifying, capturing, and storing that data; moves through the technical capability to analyze and visualize that data; and ends with an organization that is able to complement analytics with the domain knowledge of human talent and rely on a cross-functional, agile structure to implement relevant insights. The cloud is also seen as a predominant enabler of IT architecture and its modernization. Digital winners are increasingly migrating workloads and redirecting a greater share of their infrastructure spending to the cloud. However, an organization cannot capture agility benefits by simply shifting applications to cloud platforms (either private, public or in a hybrid model). Instead, the full value of cloud comes from approaching these options not as one-off tactical decisions but as part of a holistic strategy to pursue digital transformation. Capturing these benefits from cloud adoption requires more than just lift-and-shift when the business-application system configurations are heavily customized and IT processes are mostly manual. It requires a certain level of remediation to make IT systems more cloud-oriented. Bank of America has spent $25 billion, since 2010, on new technology initiatives, which includes rearchitecting "major systems," building an internal cloud, and building software with rapid speed to market. The bank is now hosting around 80 percent of its applications in its private cloud and cut the number of servers it uses to 70,000 from 200,000 with the bulk of applications running on about 8,000 servers. The cloud initiative delivered $535 million in gross savings in 2018 and enabled BofA to accelerate its "high-touch, high-tech" strategy to redesign how customers interact with its financial centers and prioritize digital banking. Ensure leadership buy-in and make accountability crystal clear – Successful organizations establish greater clarity about who is responsible for which portion of the transformation, whether it’s the ownership of a specific initiative or a particular stage in the process. Clarity about ownership is critical and the handoffs must be well-defined. There must be a clear plan for how these shifts in accountability will occur. Handoffs and overlaps are notorious friction points that are critical to manage and define. Leaders should gather the pertinent groups across the business and provide a clear plan for each transition, to avoid duplication, misalignment, and dropped balls. Moreover, the lack of leadership alignment around objectives often leads to many subscale and misaligned initiatives. One way to encourage commitment to a transformation’s initiatives is to show leaders, using pilots and proof-of-concepts, that the strategy will work. Building these proof points can galvanize support for the change effort. The same is true of increasing leaders’ digital literacy. These steps help make leaders comfortable with dedicating operating and capital expenditures at an enterprise level, which shows executive commitment and reduces the risk of wasting resources on incomplete initiatives. Digital is not just a thing that you can buy and plug into the organization. It is multi-faceted and doesn’t just involve technology. Digital transformation is an ongoing process of changing the way you do business. It requires foundational investments in skills, projects, infrastructure, and, often, in cleaning up IT systems. It requires mixing people, machines, and business processes, with all of the messiness that entails. It also requires continuous monitoring and intervention, from the top, to ensure that both digital leaders and non-digital leaders are making good decisions about their transformation efforts. "These thoughts and posts are my own"

publications.description: This article details the successful design of a two-stage deep learning aircraft engine classifier. The classifier trained on kinematic data collected from ADS-B transmissions, and significantly outperformed statistical machine learning models. The implications of this research inform other deep learning classification problems that leverage publicly available data. The full article is releasable to U.S. Government personnel and contractors.

publications.title: Reverse Engineering the Soli Radar API for Military Applications
publications.description: Hand-held and through-wall radar systems have been widely adopted for first responder safety and military applications. Current technology necessitates solutions that are expensive and bulky. Exploiting current consumer products with radar technology could achieve effects similar to what current technology provides. The example investigated is the Google Soli radar, designed for fine gesture detection to facilitate human-computer interaction. This feature is included on the Pixel 4 smartphone. Google has not publicly released the radar's application programming interface (API), making the Soli radar and its methods generally inaccessible to developers. Access to an API or a way to access information from the Soli hardware is a necessary first step in exploiting the radar for first responder and military applications. We used established reverse engineering methods to locate the packages and classes that receive information from the radar before passing it to consumer application packages within the Pixel 4. Through reverse engineering and dynamic hooking, we extracted information from the methods of the hardware abstraction layer package. The results showed it is possible to capture the Soli radar output via dynamic hooking and demonstrated its performance in detecting motion through walls.

projects.title: (Un)Clear - Seasons of Code 2021 @ IIT Bombay
projects.description: The project (Un)Clear tackles the problem of Image Super Resolution. Image super-resolution (abbrev. SR) techniques reconstruct a higher-resolution image or sequence from the observed lower-resolution images. Often a low-resolution image is taken as an input and the same image is upscaled to a higher resolution, which is the output. The details in the high-resolution output are filled in where the details are essentially unknown. Super resolution is essentially what you see in films and series like CSI where someone zooms into an image and it improves in quality and the details just appear. This project tackles Super Resolution using an advanced Deep Learning technique called ESRGAN, Enhanced Super-Resolution Generative Adversarial Networks

publications.description:
As a media coordinator at ECell, IIT Bombay, I wrote this article about the downfall and bounce-back of Microsoft. 

Like every major company, Microsoft has seen its own share of ups and downs. The company’s operating system Windows built a reputation for itself over the years. However, things started going south once the founder Bill Gates exited the company in 2000 and handed over the reins to Steve Ballmer. When Satya Nadella replaced Ballmer as the CEO 14 years later, he deployed some interesting strategies to revive Microsoft. In this blog post, we take a look at the journey of Microsoft in these years.

honorsAndAwards.title: Freedom of the City of London
honorsAndAwards.description:
On June 2nd, 2025, Lt. Hon. The Lord Mayor, Alastair King, serving as the 696th Lord Mayor of the City of London, awarded Raj the title of Freeman of the City of London. 

The prestigious Freedom of the City of London award is an esteemed honor that any individual, regardless of nationality, who has made notable contributions to public life, commerce, or the arts can be considered for.

Prior to 1996, the Freedom was open only to UK nationals and Heads of State. Since opening up the honor to non-UK nationals and non-Heads of State in 1996, approx. 100 citizens of India (and approx. 2000 non-UK citizens) have been granted the Freedom. Notable international recipients include Jawaharlal Nehru, Nelson Mandela, Margaret Thatcher, Dame Judi Dench, Florence Nightingale, Damian Lewis and many others.

projects.title: Location Assessment for Less than Truckload (LTL) Terminal Facility in The Atlanta Area
projects.description:
Collaborated with Daylight Transport, an LTL carrier, to evaluate potential locations for a new trucking terminal in Atlanta that would support the company’s operations in a cost-effective manner.

Built a GIS model that accounted for Georgia (GA) traffic patterns, trends in freight density, and location security. 

Implemented appropriate accessibility measures and computational procedures including Location Allocation and Service Area Analysis to account for the different factors of interest.

Recommended a location that is accessible within 2 hours to 60% of GA potential market which is equivalent to an average of  $431 million and $258.5 in 2018 Pick Up and Delivery revenues respectively.

projects.title: Data Analytics and Optimization Towards Improving Efficiency and Performance of Longhaul LTL Operations
projects.description:
Formulated and implemented a rolling horizon optimization algorithm for re-structuring the existing operational network of Daylight Transport, an LTL (less than truck load) carrier based in Long Beach, California.

Customized a scheduling formulation to support the network planning algorithm. The scheduling formulation is targeted at minimizing lead-times and irregular service requests.   

Drafted and presented weekly updates on the development of the computational procedures and the resulting findings.

Established 10 new routes that are estimated to save $1.1 million in annual operations. 

Increased the fraction of shipments served by dedicated fleets from 45% to 60%. These were previously served by higher cost non-dedicated (procured) fleets.

projects.title: Short-term Traffic Forecasting to Support Dynamic Traffic System Management Interventions
projects.description:
Developed, implemented, and evaluated of a methodology to identify demand driven perturbations in traffic flow and integrated them in traffic state predictive tools. 

The predictive model performs within a rolling horizon framework to support Active Transportation and Demand Management (ATDM) and Dynamic Mobility Applications (DMA) interventions.

The core of this prediction model is Approximate Bayesian Computation (ABC), and it is tested in different scenarios using historical traffic data and demand triggers from external data sources (such as Twitter). 

The performance of the presented model is compared to other methods, ARIMA, Sample Moving Average, and Standard Bayesian. The results indicate that ABC quickly adjusts to drastic changes in flow levels, and that it results in acceptable predictions for the different time periods.

This project is based in part on research funded by the Office of Operations Research and Development, Federal Highway Administration, US Department of Transportation, and conducted in collaboration with Leidos. Inc

projects.title: Performance evaluation of a complex infrastructure system: a study of the effects of airport improvements on flight delays
projects.description:
We evaluated an expansion project of one of the top three US airports in terms of total passenger boardings.

The study used graphical analyses and statistical models to examine the relation between runway additions and reconfiguration and various measures of airline operational delays. 

The effects of trends in aircraft operations volumes, airline-initiated flight schedule adjustments, and the incidence of instrument weather conditions were tested as confounders. 

Results suggested that while some of the investment goals were achieved, as expected, investments have not yet produced reductions in some measures of delays, and, in fact, some delay metrics have worsened.

projects.title: Freight Forecasting with a Novel Reinforcement Learning Framework
projects.description:
We developed a demand forecasting methodology in R to support freight operation planning over short to medium term horizons. 

The methodology combined traditional time series models and machine learning algorithms in a reinforcement learning framework. 

The objective was to find an efficient method that reduced the prediction error. 

The model was developed for one of the top US intermodal companies. It was tested on their 2013 to 2017 shipment data. 

The model succeeded in reducing the forecast error margin. It also allowed predictions to follow recent trends and fluctuations in the market while minimizing the user intervention.

projects.title: Information Updating Using Mobile Drones for Robust Relief Routing and Distribution in Disaster Areas
projects.description:
There are multiple examples in which failure of the road network hindered relief operations. The developed model used a dynamic programming approach to solve the relief routing problem while taking into account the changing state of the infrastructure.

To achieve this, we proposed deploying inexpensive drones along with trucks. The drones then equip decision makers with two additional pieces of information regarding the state of the road network ahead and the fleet and relief supplies. 

The real time information then helped update the routing plan accordingly, and the program sought paths with maximum reliability. 

The model included a math program that solved for the optimal package distribution. 

The model was tested on earthquake-prone Ercis, a town in Turkey. The results showed that there was value in the information transmitted by drones especially when the network state was highly uncertain.

projects.title: Urban Transport in Greater Beirut: Analysis of Economic Costs and Solutions
projects.associatedWith: Associated with American University of Beirut
projects.description:
We collaborated with researchers from the World Bank on an urban transport study for Beirut, Lebanon.

The study analyzed a number of supply side and demand side measures that may reduce congestion in Greater Beirut Area.

We identified the different transport challenges in Greater Beirut from rapid motorization to inadequate transport infrastructure and high concentration of jobs and population .

We led the effort in collecting supply and demand side data to characterize travel. The data included information on the infrastructure, modes available, public transport options and state, costs, travel time, number of peak and off peak period trips, and land use.

I’ve always been driven by curiosity — about how things work, how systems connect, and how data can tell a story that leads to better decisions. For me, it’s not just about solving problems—it’s about building lasting solutions and helping others grow along the way.

projects.title: Utilization of Mechanically Simulated Kangaroo Care as a Novel Homeostatic Method to Promote Healthy Development in Mus musculus as a Model for Human Preterm Neonates
projects.description: Globally, prematurity is the leading cause of death for newborns; approximately one million children die each year due to complications of preterm birth. This project develops a novel method to promote healthier development in neonates by utilizing mechanically simulated kangaroo care for Mus musculus neonates as a model for humans. A majority of premature babies are treated with traditional maternal kangaroo care, however, this method isn’t always possible as it requires the attention of a mother for at least one consecutive hour. The potential for mechanically simulated kangaroo care opens the doors for a treatment technique that does not require the mother and can be implemented for extended periods of time. In this research, three groups of five mice were randomly assigned to a treatment group of 0, 1, or 2 hours of mechanically simulated kangaroo care. The mice were tested for levels of mobility, heart rate, temperature, body weight, and scored based on the body condition scoring technique. After 21 days, the mice groups followed a positive relationship where increased hours exposed to kangaroo care led to increased mobility, less variable heart rates, healthier body weights and body scores, and stabilized temperature. Based on these results, this project suggests that mechanically simulated kangaroo care was able to promote healthier development in Mus musculus neonates and provided insight into the positive impact of mechanically simulated kangaroo care on human preterm neonates. It is inferred that these positive impacts were observed as a result of the calming effect of kangaroo care that decreases the sympathetic and parasympathetic nervous system components of heart rate variability and stabilizes long-term heart rates, summarized as increased homeostasis.

projects.title: Statistical Analysis for Population Ecology:  Mitigation of Invasive Lionfish (Pterois volitans/miles)
projects.description:
This project takes an innovative approach to quell the infestation of Indo-Pacific Lionfish in
Florida waters by investigating mathematical population modeling techniques and attempting to
find a connection between these models that leads to an extensive plan to help mitigate
invasive lionfish. Using a robust multi-model approach, the first goal was to estimate a baseline
population of lionfish in each Florida location. Due to the simplicity of lionfish population
dynamics such as their lack of migration, Hayne’s method is an accurate technique to find a
population estimate. Afterwards, the second goal of determining the probability of capture was
accomplished using a multinomial method. This probability value was tested for accuracy by
comparing the population estimate for the multinomial method with the population estimate from
Hayne’s method assuming a standard error for the estimate. If the model passes the standard
error test, then the probability values were deemed as accurate and were compared. This
multinomial method was tested for 10 different locations under 5 different conditions of 1, 2, 3,
4, and 5 trapping events. An analysis of these statistical models coupled with a depletion model
indicates that there is a correlation between less trapping events and a more optimal rate of
return, postulating a more efficient and cost-effective mitigation method if it utilizes less trapping
events that are more intensive compared to more trappings which are less intensive. This
analysis can be extended to a multitude of other invasive species proliferation problems.

projects.title: Determining the Effect of a Top-Level Predator in a Simulated Aquatic  Ecosystem with Organisms Used for the Mitigation of HABs
projects.description:
Harmful Algae Blooms (HAB) have caused over 1 billion dollars in ecological damages coupled
with the dangerous environmental problem of perpetuating non-natural mitigation methods
that destroy the world’s waterways. This is why biological mitigation methods such as the
introduction of predator species are used to reduce that cost. The purpose of the research is to
determine the effect that a top-level predator (Ghost Shrimp) will have on an ecosystem with
different organisms (Brachionus, Cladocera, Philodina, Tardigrades, and Cyclops Copepods) for
the mitigation of Blue-Green Algae. It will also be determined which organism will work best
with the top-level predator in a synergistic relationship in order to control Harmful Algae
Blooms. A predator-prey relationship model is developed from the program PhysioDesigner, in
order to determine the optimal amount of each organism that can be used in the real-life
model of an ecosystem. From this optimal amount of organisms, a real-life ecosystem model
was built with different combinations of the top-level predator with each organism against
algae compared to just the organisms against algae in order to determine the effectiveness of
each combination and the effectiveness of the introduction of a top-level predator. The results
are significant because it shows that a top-level predator (Ghost Shrimp) can affect the
ecosystem by regulating the population of the primary consumer (each organism) and that the
most optimal combination of species for the mitigation of harmful Blue-Green Algae is Ghost
Shrimp with Brachionus.

projects.title: Deriving a predator-prey model for regulating the growth of HABs with different species of zooplankton inside of a water ecological system
projects.description: Did you know that harmful algae blooms produce cyanotoxins that can potentially harm animals and humans? The purpose of this research is to make a predator-prey relationship model that will determine the amount of two zooplankton species needed to regulate growth of blue-green algae and prevent occurrence of harmful algal blooms, and to compare the data from the models with experimental data of 2 different species of zooplankton interacting with blue-green algae. The developed model simulates 3 different species, 2 predators (rotifers and copepods) and 1 prey (algae) to predict the outcomes of a simple ecosystem. Derivations of the basic Lotka-Volterra predator-prey equations are used in the PhysioDesigner modeling software to develop a predator-prey model where an ecosystem is at equilibrium. The final equations were developed which resulted in a final balanced ecosystem where all the species stabilizes. The results are significant because it shows that ecological models can be used to help find a way of controlling harmful algae blooms using zooplankton predators in a balanced natural ecosystem.

projects.title: A comparison of deterministic and stochastic numerical models for climate forecasting
projects.description: Did you know that no two weather patterns are alike, although people will say that a particular day is similar to one they experienced in the past? The hypothesis states that if different numerical weather prediction models are compared, then data will show that the stochastic models will be better as a weather prediction model compared to deterministic models. The hypothesis was tested by obtaining the temperature predictions from the GEFS, SREF, NAM, and CMC models for 24 hours at hourly intervals from ten different locations (Juneau, Melbourne, Los Angeles, Honolulu, Chicago, Minneapolis, Kansas City, New York, Houston, and Seattle). Then the predictions were compared to actual temperature readings. After comparing the temperature predictions to the actual readings, the total error was calculated and compared. The variables were: Independent-temperature models, Dependent-temperature values, and controls were the locations and time interval. During experimentation, it was observed that the GEFS model predicted the most accurate temperature, and the CMC model predicted the least accurate temperature compared to the actual recordings. Based on the hourly trials, the GEFS model which is a stochastic model was the best model for predicting temperature; the average amount of error for the GEFS was 25 degrees. The CMC model which is a deterministic model was the worst model for predicting temperature; the average amount of error for the CMC was 50 degrees. The data and results supported the hypothesis, which shows that the stochastic models predicted the most accurate temperatures when compared to actual temperature readings.

publications.title: In vivo structure profiling reveals human cytosolic and mitochondrial tRNA structurome and interactome in response to stress
publications.description: Transfer RNA (tRNA) is the most abundant cellular RNA family in terms of copy numbers. It not only folds into defined structures but also has complex cellular interaction networks involving aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases, translation factors, and ribosomes. The human tRNAome is comprised of chromosomal-encoded tRNAs with a large sequence diversity and mitochondrial-encoded tRNAs with A/U-rich sequences and noncanonical tertiary interactions. How tRNA folding and interactions in a eukaryotic cell respond to stress is poorly understood. Here, we develop DM-DMS-MaPseq, which utilizes in vivo dimethyl-sulfate (DMS) chemical probing and mutational profiling (MaP) coupled with demethylase (DM) treatment in transcriptome-wide tRNA sequencing to profile structures and the cellular interactions of human chromosomal and mitochondrial-encoded tRNAs. We found that tRNAs maintain stable structures in vivo, but the in vivo DMS profiles are vastly different from those in vitro, which can be explained by their interactions with cellular proteins and the ribosome. We also identify cytosolic and mitochondrial tRNA structure and interaction changes upon arsenite treatment, a type of oxidative stress that induces translational reprogramming, which is consistent with global translation repression in both compartments. Our results reveal variations of tRNA structurome and dynamic interactome that have functional consequences in translational regulation.

publications.title: Quantification of tRNA m1A modification by templated-ligation qPCR
publications.description: N1-methyladenosine (m1A) is a widespread modification in all eukaryotic, many archaeal, and some bacterial tRNAs. M1A is generally located in the T loop of cytosolic tRNA and between acceptor and D stems of mitochondrial tRNAs, it is involved in tertiary interaction that stabilizes tRNA. Human tRNA m1A levels are dynamically regulated that fine-tune translation and can also serve as biomarkers for infectious disease. Although many methods have been used to measure m1A, a PCR method to assess m1A levels quantitatively in specific tRNAs has been lacking. Here we develop a templated-ligation followed by qPCR method (TL-qPCR) that measures m1A levels in target tRNAs. Our method uses the SplintR ligase that efficiently ligates two tRNA complementary DNA oligonucleotides using tRNA as the template followed by qPCR using the ligation product as the template. M1A interferes with the ligation in specific ways, allowing for the quantitative assessment of m1A levels using sub-nanogram amounts of total RNA. We identify the features of specificity and quantitation for m1A modified model RNAs and apply these to total RNA samples from human cells. Our method enables easy access to study the dynamics and function of this pervasive tRNA modification.

publications.title: tRNA flux and consistency in differentiation
publications.description: tRNA transcriptome composition and regulation are poorly understood. A study reports tRNA transcriptome reprogramming during human cell differentiation, where the abundance of individual tRNA gene transcripts is drastically changed, but each pool of tRNAs containing the same anticodon remains stable.

publications.title: Engineered mischarged transfer RNAs for correcting pathogenic missense mutations
publications.description: Missense mutations account for approximately 50% of pathogenic mutations in human genetic diseases, and most lack effective treatments. Gene therapies, gene editing, and RNA therapies, including transfer RNA (tRNA) modalities, are common strategies for genetic disease treatments. However, reported tRNA therapies are for nonsense mutations only. It has not been explored how tRNAs can be engineered to correct missense mutations. Here, we describe missense-correcting tRNAs (mc-tRNAs) as a potential therapeutic for correcting pathogenic missense mutations. Mc-tRNAs are engineered tRNAs charged with one amino acid, but read codons of another in translation. We first developed a series of fluorescent protein-based reporters that indicate the successful correction of missense mutations via restoration of fluorescence. We engineered mc-tRNAs that effectively corrected serine and arginine missense mutations in the reporters and confirmed the amino acid substitution by mass spectrometry and mc-tRNA expression by sequencing. We examined the transcriptome response to mc-tRNA expression and found some mc-tRNAs induced minimum transcriptomic changes. Furthermore, we applied an mc-tRNA to rescue a pathogenic CAPN3 Arg-to-Gln mutant involved in LGMD2A. These results establish a versatile pipeline for mc-tRNA engineering and demonstrate the potential of mc-tRNA as an alternative therapeutic platform for the treatment of genetic disorders.

publications.title: Profiling lariat intermediates reveals genetic determinants of early and late co-transcriptional splicing
publications.description: Long introns with short exons in vertebrate genes are thought to require spliceosome assembly across exons (exon definition), rather than introns, thereby requiring transcription of an exon to splice an upstream intron. Here, we developed CoLa-seq (co-transcriptional lariat sequencing) to investigate the timing and determinants of co-transcriptional splicing genome wide. Unexpectedly, 90% of all introns, including long introns, can splice before transcription of a downstream exon, indicating that exon definition is not obligatory for most human introns. Still, splicing timing varies dramatically across introns, and various genetic elements determine this variation. Strong U2AF2 binding to the polypyrimidine tract predicts early splicing, explaining exon definition-independent splicing. Together, our findings question the essentiality of exon definition and reveal features beyond intron and exon length that are determinative for splicing timing.

publications.title: IoT Socioenvironmental Assessment Instrument: Validation Process Applying Delphi Method
publications.description:
🔹Industry 4.0 technologies offer significant opportunities to enhance sustainable production and circular economy practices in the face of challenges arising from climate change.

🔹Considering the growing interest in this field, the literature review exposed that, particularly in the case of the Internet of Things (IoT), there is a need for empirical assessments of the impact of this technology on sustainability and circularity.

🔹This paper presents the validation process of an original assessment tool that evaluates IoT’s alignment with the socioenvironmental and circular context of manufacturing organizations and their supply chains.

🔹Emphasis is placed on the construct titled “𝘐𝘰𝘛 𝘛𝘦𝘤𝘩𝘯𝘰𝘭𝘰𝘨𝘺 𝘌𝘹𝘱𝘦𝘤𝘵𝘢𝘵𝘪𝘰𝘯𝘴”. After systematically conducting a literature review, this study employed the Delphi method in conjunction with statistical analyses to refine or formulate new indicators or statements based on expert consensus, validating the proposed assessment tool.

🔹The findings of this research contribute to management practices by providing an instrument to assess the current stance of top management and other key managers (production, project and supply chain) on IoT use in manufacturing operations or supply chains from a socioenvironmental and circular perspective.

🔹The instrument serves as a starting point for exploring IoT’s potential in circular economy practices. Academically, it provides a detailed explanation of the Delphi method and its application and outcomes.

receivedRecommendations.givenByHeadline: Vice President for Student Development
receivedRecommendations.givenAt: August 31, 2016, Paul was Morgan’s mentor
receivedRecommendations.description:
I enthusiastically write a letter of recommendation for Morgan Jacob.  I worked with Morgan over a two year period of time.  In the 2014-15 academic year, she served the Wheaton College community as the Executive Vice President for College Life and was a representative to the College Committee on Student Publications, a committee I chair.  In the 2015-16 academic year, Morgan served as the Vice President of Student Government.  We met every two weeks throughout the 2015-16 academic year and collaborated on a number of critical issues.

When I first met her, she communicated an immediate sense of self-confidence.  Morgan used her self-confidence to get to know me.  She asked the kind of question that communicated genuine interest and care in me as a person as well as respect for my position of leadership.  Morgan’s wit and humor, in combination with her self-confident initiative made her approachable.

The first year I knew Morgan, we served together on the student publications governing committee.  That particular year, we needed to make a number of changes to the constitution and also review a difficult issue related to the student newspaper.  Morgan came prepared to meetings and engaged with faculty and administrative leaders as well as with her student peers with respect.  She listened effectively, and articulated her perspective clearly while remaining open to dissenting perspectives.  

The second year I knew Morgan, the College experienced one of its greatest challenges I have witnessed in my 18 years.  When the Board of Trustees decided to assemble a review team to reflect on this intense two month period of time, which included three campus protests and continuous debate in social media as well as in news reports worldwide, they asked Morgan to represent a students’ perspective by serving on the review team.  I do not know of another undergraduate student in my 24 years of working in higher education that was trusted more at the highest levels of leadership at a College with such a sensitive and weighty responsibility.  The Trustee appointment of Morgan to their review team was a significant endorsement of her ability to work collaboratively with others and to manage incredible pressure without losing perspective.  

Morgan is able to effectively address problems.  Morgan was a key voice in revising the student publication constitution during the 14-15 academic year.  She was also a key voice in helping the College respond to student body unrest from mid-December, 2015 to mid-February, 2016, in part, by helping to plan and to host an open forum for students with the College President and Provost, and in part by serving on the Trustee review task force.   

I can say with confidence that Morgan will be an asset to any organization with which she serves.  
Sincerely,
Paul O. Chelsen
Vice President for Student Development

headline: Associate Partner at Bain & Company | ex-Amazon
about:
I am an Associate Partner with Bain & Company in their Washington D.C. office (~10 years with Bain). I spend most of my time at the intersection of Consumer Goods/Retail and customer strategy / data and AI / marketing / M&A serving global clients across North America, Europe, and APAC. 

I have an MBA from The University of Chicago Booth School of Business. Over the summer while at Booth, I worked as a Senior Product Manager with Amazon.com at their HQ in Seattle. 

I did my undergrad in Materials Science and Engineering at the Indian Institute of Technology, Bombay, graduating at the top of my class. I hold a patent. I spent a summer working with superconductors at the Ecole Polytechnique Federale de Lausanne in Switzerland. 

Outside of work, I'm currently trying to keep up with my two little kids. I've spent vacations road-tripping across the US, having also done the cross-country drive from LA to DC along the historic Route 66. You'll catch me drinking beer, or scotch. I love NPR, dogs, biking, and Formula 1. I'm an avid hiker and have completed over 50 treks in the Himalayas, Alps, Andes, the Jura mountains, and the Inca trail to Machu Picchu. I'm a certified scuba diver, but don't dive as much as I'd like to. Next on my list is learning how to sail.

honorsAndAwards.description:
Booth '21 Graduating Class recipient of the Rattan L. Khosa "Against All Odds" Student Entrepreneurship Awards.

This award is open to any Full-Time, Evening, or Weekend MBA Program student graduating within the 2020-2021 academic year who has overcome significant obstacles and demonstrated a spirit of entrepreneurship to launch or significantly grow a new venture. This student will have benefited greatly from Polsky Center programs and the entrepreneurship curriculum to advance the venture. The venture should have an established revenue stream and sustainable business model and be poised for growth post-graduation. While there is no minimum GPA required, the student must have achieved the entrepreneurship concentration and shown leadership at Booth and in the greater business community.

The sponsor of this award is Rattan L. Khosa, ’79. Rattan’s entrepreneurial story demonstrates significant hard work and perseverance. Rattan first came to the United States from his native India with just $3.25 in his pocket, and in 1981 started AMSYSCO, a company that provides post-tensioning systems on commercial structures, out of his basement. Overcoming countless hurdles, Rattan has grown AMSYSCO into a highly profitable company that today captures some 70% market share.

about:
Expert Associate Partner in Bain & Company's Coro team.

Previously an Associate Fellow at the Kavli Institute for Cosmological Physics (KICP) at the University of Chicago, studying the detection of ultra-high energy cosmic rays via the showers of secondary particles they produce when they interact with the earth's atmosphere.
I was a member of the Pierre Auger Collaboration (www.auger.org), and was heavily involved in the development of a next-generation air fluorescence detector - the Fluorescence detector Array of Single-pixel Telescopes (www.fast-project.org). I also ran the KICP's Life Long Learning program - an outreach initiative in which we sent researchers to give public lectures to older adults in libraries and senior centers around Chicago.

My most recent publications are listed here:

headline: Partner at Bain & Company
about:
Evren Sungur is a leader in Bain's Performance Improvement practice and leads Bain's Corporate Support solution in the Americas. He advises senior executives on cost and strategic transformations that deliver measurable near-term results and build capabilities to sustain performance over time. He has worked across industries with deep experience in Retail. In addition to corporate clients, he has advised numerous private equity funds on commercial due diligence and portfolio company value creation planning.

Clients consistently cite Evren’s pragmatic, results-driven style. A Fortune 500 CFO described his work as “the highest ROI investment for the company,” and another Fortune 500 CEO called the work as “the best consulting work he has seen in his career.”

Beyond his case work, Evren leads Bain Boston recruiting efforts for The University of Chicago Booth School of Business. He is also the Building Entrepreneurial Leaders program manager for Bain Boston.

Evren holds an MBA from the University of Chicago Booth School of Business and M.A./B.A. degrees from Brandeis University. He is a graduate of the United World College USA.

Outside of Bain, he enjoys spending time with his wife and two sons, playing basketball and freediving. He and his family support the Boston Children’s Museum and Massachusetts General Hospital cancer research efforts.

about:

Previously, I led client engagements across customer-centric transformations, enterprise strategy, and operating model redesigns. My work has helped executive teams unlock growth, improve supply chains, launch Agile teams, and conduct rigorous commercial due diligences for private equity firms.

As a people leader, I’ve managed multidisciplinary teams, served as a professional development advisor for seven consultants, and mentored many others—reflecting a long-standing commitment to talent development.

I hold an MBA from the University of Chicago Booth School of Business, where I graduated with high honors, and a B.S. in Business Administration with a second major in Economics from the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, where I graduated summa cum laude.

From the Cognitive Neuroscience Lab:

"Evidence from Neuropsychology suggests that anterograde amnesia, which can occur following damage to midline diencephalic or medial temporal brain regions, involves a disruption of recollection while sparing priming. Many theoretical explanations for this dissociation have been put forward. One possibility is that amnesia arises due to a disruption of a special process ("cross-cortical consolidation"), that is specifically required for memory storage with respect to facts and events. publications.description:
Bain and Company partner Mikey Vu estimates meal kits comprise at least $1.5 billion of the $850 billion U.S. grocery market. He explained to CNBC that there's plenty of room for growth.

"We estimate [meal kit] awareness is as high as half the general grocery shopping population, but that trial rate is still pretty low (~6%)," Vu told CNBC in an email. "We see significant opportunity for growth over the next several years, potentially more than 50 percent market growth in the next 6-7 years."

publications.title: Peapod arms itself as grocery wars intensify
publications.description:
As Amazon and Walmart push their way into consumers' online grocery carts, Peapod—the elder statesman of the industry—is fighting back. But it won't be easy to win long term.

"E-commerce is exceptionally expensive and hard to make money on, especially as customer expectations have risen," says Mikey Vu, a partner with Bain & Company. Free same-day delivery timed to the minute is "incredibly hard to do. For Peapod, it's even harder because they don't have the scale of Amazon."

publications.title: Amazon's Whole Foods Price Cuts Brought 25% Jump in Shoppers

publications.title: Amazon's Whole Foods deal will make Alexa a lot smarter
publications.description: Amazon already has access to troves of consumer data. People can buy everything from books to furniture on its website. However, Amazon had one blind spot: grocery, said Mikey Vu, a partner with Bain & Company.

publications.title: Grocery stores are fighting back against meal kit companies
publications.description: Meal kit sales account for only $1.5 billion of the $800 billion grocery business, according to Mikey Vu, a partner with Bain & Company. But new companies are popping up, hoping to capture a piece of what could be a quickly growing business.

publications.title: Food Giants Say They're Ready for Amazon, But Wall Street Is Skeptical

Upstart brands, restaurants and meal-kit services have taken some market share. But often consumers are just paying lower prices, making it harder for the big food companies to maintain growth.

“There’s a shift in trust to the retailer brands,” said Mikey Vu, a grocery expert at Bain & Co. “That has to scare the heck out of the national brands.”

publications.title: The Price War Over American Groceries Is Getting Bloody

headline: Consultant at Bain & Company | Chicago Booth MBA ’25
about:
After graduating from high school, Kevin Hernandez sought opportunities to work in public education, driven by a desire to help under-resourced communities overcome systemic barriers. He began his career with Academica, the largest educational service provider in the United States, where he discovered a passion for the EdTech space. Through his work at Academica, Kevin developed a deep understanding of public education—what works, what needs to change, and what must be done to ensure students have access to a better education and a more equitable chance at achieving their dreams.

At Williams College, Kevin continued his commitment to equity in education by working with the First-Generation Advisory Board, serving as a Junior Advisor, and partnering with the Dean’s Office to better support students whose voices had historically been underrepresented.

More recently, Kevin completed a two-year commitment with Teach For America, where he experienced firsthand the transformative potential of technology in schools when implemented effectively. Witnessing the impact of technological innovation on his students reinforced his belief that technology can play a critical role in breaking oppressive cycles and empowering every student—regardless of race, socioeconomic status, sexual orientation, or other identities—to succeed. His long-term goal is to help students understand that their dreams are achievable and that they have the resources to pursue them.

Kevin earned his MBA from the University of Chicago Booth School of Business in 2025. He is currently a Consultant at Bain & Company in San Francisco, where he works in the Private Equity practice.

featured.subtitle: Weiwen Han on LinkedIn

slides.title: 企业韧性的三大误区
slides.subtitle: Weiwen Han on LinkedIn
slides.description: 大多数行业受到外部冲击的次数和严重程度都在不断增加，效率至上反而令企业更易受到冲击。疫情之下，越来越多的企业高管表示愿意投资提升企业韧性。 文 | 韩微文 贝恩公司大中华区总裁，全球董事会成员 疫情新常态下，在中国，许多企业已经从保护业务（Protect）、恢复业务（Recover），逐渐步入到“利用危机开启战略重塑”阶段，力求实现结构化转型和模式上的升级（Retool）。 去年，我曾谈到，第三阶段对CEO提出了全新的要求，CEO必须合理分配资源，帮助企业不断提高“预测能力”、“适应能力”和“企业韧性”。（详见《后疫情时代，CEO打造未来企业的战略方针》） 其中，企业韧性是最近关注度非常高的一个话题。随着全球化的深入发展、不平等现象的加剧、新技术带来新的风险，以及气候变化带来更频繁与更极端的灾害事件影响，企业所面临的复杂局面正在进一步发酵。无论什么行业，企业对韧性的重视程度都在显著提升。 然而，越来越多的证据表明，企业长期以来秉承的风险管理原则在如今或许已经不再适用。即使有些企业凭借员工和合作伙伴共同付出的巨大努力，成功度过了当前疫情危机，它们同样意识到有必要引入一个更可持续的方法。 正如几年前急于全面数字化一样，许多关于企业韧性的讨论并不深入。在最近与企业家的对话中，贝恩发现存在关于企业韧性的三大严重误区，走出这些误区将是提高企业韧性的第一步。 误区1：唯资产负债表论 高管们往往仅通过资产负债表衡量韧性，检查杠杆率和流动性，却忽视了其他导致组织脆弱性的潜在原因。事实上，韧性的衡量包括以下五个维度： 战略韧性，包括绝对规模和相对规模、需求弹性、营收和利润多元化以及互相关关系 财务韧性，包括杠杆率和流动性，也包括保险覆盖和对冲手段 运营韧性，包括经营杠杆率、供应商集中度和库存余量 技术韧性，包括技术可得性、工作量的灵活性和网络安全 组织韧性，包括危机应急准备、组织敏捷性和个人韧性 从全局来看，会发现外部事件通常会从以上多个维度同时影响企业，加剧冲击程度。综合考虑将有助于高管们做出更明智的决策，集中稀缺资源，着力提升韧性。例如，新冠疫情期间，由于供应链过于复杂且缺乏透明度，许多企业陷入了零部件短缺的困境，而此前它们没能意识到这一问题的严重性。 误区2：提高韧性无需额外投入 企业可以在不牺牲目前盈利水平的情况下提升韧性，例如提高供应链的透明度或引入危机防范机制。然而，要想在韧性方面获得显著优势，企业必然需要额外投资和付出机会成本。 贝恩认为，企业领导们应扩大与投资者的对话范围，以平衡短期和长期价值创造。树立统一而客观的衡量标准是第一步。 对此，贝恩基于危机期间企业的业绩表现和各项易于观测的指标（包括：企业规模、增速、利润率、资产密度、杠杆率、流动性以及地域和产品集中度）之间的统计关系，建立了满分为100分的“贝恩韧性指数”，有助于与投资者展开以事实为基础的对话。我们的研究发现，尽管高风险可以带来高回报，从长期来看，高韧性企业的存活率几乎是低韧性企业的近两倍。 误区3：韧性归风险部门管 很多时候，风险管理被认为是一种强制性但又流于形式的工作，最后被遗忘在边缘地带。一旦接受这种狭隘的范围设定，风险部门就有可能在识别风险时变得过于关注战术（而非战略）且无法保持客观。 在这个企业所面临的不确定性加剧的年代，许多风险的组合特性要求企业识别并降低整个企业的风险。针对特定职能部门和业务单位零星地采取特定的风控措施，可能无法使整个企业的韧性水平达到要求。此外，未来的许多风险将来自企业外部合作伙伴的生态系统，传统的风险管理部门无法应对这一挑战。 企业需要提升对风险的重视程度，并将其纳入最高领导层和董事会的关键决策节奏和流程中。各级领导在制定决策时，应发挥主人翁精神，充分考虑决策将如何影响整个企业的长期价值创造，而不是主要关注增长潜力和仅仅防范那些不会互相影响的风险领域。 CEO如何锻造企业韧性？ 建立合适的组织韧性水平和类型，需要结合长期愿景、对企业和行业经济的深刻理解以及出众的创新能力。综上，CEO可以采取“三步走”的方法，开启企业韧性建设之路。 1、评估企业风险敞口 首先，需要对企业主要弱点的性质和程度进行严格、以事实为基础的分析。一方面，运用事实数据确定所在行业和企业的利润驱动因素。另一方面，设计对标分析，从而更好地了解企业相对于竞争对手的韧性表现。同时，建立压力测试模型，确定企业能够承担的最大风险，同时确保将二阶效应考虑在内。 2、就具体的风险偏好达成一致 CEO应当推动高管团队和董事会就企业韧性的长期表现达成共识，并就未来的风险容忍度达成一致。通过解决难点问题获得充分信息，并据此制定具体目标，谨防流于表面、没有充分投入的做法。 3、 制定战略规划并赢得投资者青睐 将易于实现的目标和高收益的投资相结合，以此为基础拟定韧性发展议程。全程邀请投资者参与，通过重新打磨公司投资亮点，让投资者了解转型的过程，以展现新举措如何在经济周期中实现股东价值最大化。 放眼未来，在黑天鹅事件频发、竞争模式升级的时代背景下，提升企业韧性将成为企业长青的重要因素。CEO们应当立即采取行动，先人一步，赢在未来。 在接下来的总裁专栏中，我将从CEO如何提高企业的“预测能力”和“适应能力”两个维度，带来更多深入的洞察与建议。 注：本文首发于韩微文先生在福布斯的个人专栏 原文链接：https://www.forbeschina.com/business/55139

slides.title: 点燃企业的“第二引擎”
slides.subtitle: Weiwen Han on LinkedIn
slides.description: 成功点燃“第二引擎”的企业，他们的领导者往往拥有初创公司般的创业精力。但相比初创企业，这些企业又能够利用已有的规模效应优势，更加快速地实现规模化，达到快速增长的战略意图。 文 | 韩微文 贝恩公司大中华区总裁，全球董事会成员 多年以来，贝恩始终致力于探究企业实现持续盈利性增长的秘诀。过去25年里，贝恩全球战略专家运用我们掌握的各类工具，经过大量研究和分析，撰写了《回归核心》（Profit from the Core）一书。书中提出， 90%以上的大型企业成功的秘诀是专注于自己的核心优势业务（即“第一引擎”），凭借不断创新、优化可重复的模式，不停扩大业务范围，从而占据领先地位，发挥经济效应。 然而，近十年以来，商业环境发生了改变。贝恩动荡指数（用于衡量主要趋势和事件的相对量级）显示，我们正进入一个市场长期不稳定的新阶段，而上一个相似量级的阶段则是一战到二战结束时。置身纷繁复杂的商业环境，企业想要实现持续盈利的难度越来越大：目前，十家企业里只有一家能够连续10年保持平均水准以上的盈利性增长。而过去10年中，有8家企业所创造的正向市场价值是全球3000家顶尖上市公司总价值的15%。 通过分析最成功的持续增长企业案例，我们发现，成功企业不再仅仅局限于增强“第一引擎”的实力，而是提前转型并点燃了企业的“第二引擎”。 什么是“第二引擎”？ “第二引擎”指的是企业利用已有的规模效应，即“第一引擎”的资产和能力，在内部开创新业务（组织自建或通过收购）。 贝恩发现，成功点燃“第二引擎”的企业，他们的领导者往往拥有初创公司般的创业精力。但相比初创企业，这些企业又能够利用已有的规模效应优势，更加快速地实现规模化，达到快速增长的战略意图（图1）。 图1 “第二引擎”业务利用现有的核心业务的资产和能力实现快速增长的目标 通过研究分析100个大型企业的成功案例，贝恩总结出以下三种“第二引擎”的业务类型： 类型1：更新换代“第一引擎” 研究中，有近三分之一的企业通过更新换代“第一引擎”，满足同一批客户的类似需求，取得“第二引擎”的连续成功。我们发现，这类“第二引擎”适合变化相对缓慢的行业，如能源、医疗等。在新技术的推动下，这些企业或将面临着具有颠覆性的新兴行业竞争者，对“第一引擎”产生威胁。有三分之二的受访高管认为，他们五年后最担心的竞争对手将会与现在不同。 例如，以生产石油和气体为第一引擎的壳牌从2015年起将“可再生能源”作为公司的第二引擎，不仅成立了一个独立的部门进军可再生能源市场，还通过一系列收购和合资建设专业能力，取得显著增长。星展银行从2014年开始启动以“数字化转型”为核心的第二引擎，在公司内部鼓励创始人精神和敏捷思维，并重新部署人才发展第二引擎，取得了良好的效果。 类型2：发展与“第一引擎”关联性较弱的业务 研究中，有约一半的企业属于此类“第二引擎”。技术进步、业务边界融合，以及不断涌现的新竞争方式，让固定资本投资相对较低的企业降低了准入门槛，让企业有机会以全新的方式重新发挥“第一引擎”的作用和潜力。 例如，2003年，以二次充电电池起家的比亚迪通过收购秦川汽车，开启了它的第二引擎——汽车制造，并利用在锂电子电池生产上的核心优势，早早打开了电动车市场的大门。随着中国消费者饮食习惯的变化，2017年百胜中国通过收购到家，打造以送餐服务为核心的第二引擎，推出了全新的品牌移动端APP，为消费者提供便利的数字化体验。 类型3：进军全新的业务领域 这类企业选择开创与“第一引擎”无关的全新“第二引擎”，通过改变核心资产和能力，进军新业务领域，并为新业务提供规模化支持。 例如，永辉超市从2011年起开始与数字原生企业合作，对原先以本地杂货经营为主门店进行改革，按照顾客需求分为经济实惠的“红标店”（第一引擎）和针对高端人群的“绿标店”(第二引擎)，包括旗下Bravo精标店、永辉超级物种等。与此同时，永辉通过线上线下运营，不断提升全渠道能力；通过与生态系统内的伙伴合作，获取采购、供应链、物流等方面的新能力，永辉强大的采购能力和成熟的冷链网络是其能够提供侧重生鲜的差异化产品的坚实后盾。 如何打造成功的“第二引擎” 如今的外部环境条件，为企业打造“第二引擎”提供了有利的条件。经过研究，贝恩为CEO总结了打造“第二引擎”的四个关键成功要素（图二）。 能够使用“第一引擎”业务的主要资产和能力，在企业内部建立和拓展业务 营造“创始人精神”的创业环境，树立鲜明的文化和运营模式，建立规模化业务 获取竞争优势新杠杆，降低原本关联性不大或受到严密防护的市场进入门槛 瞄准规模庞大且不断增长的市场和利润池 图2 几乎每一个成功的“第二引擎”在四个主要因素上表现卓著 当今世界资本充足，企业更容易收购具备关键能力的公司，也更容易建立技术合作关系。而随着无形资产的增加，人才重新分配的频率和速度大大提高，我们相信，未来，“第二引擎”的故事将会更富吸引力。 注：本文首发于韩微文先生在福布斯的个人专栏 原文链接：https://www.forbeschina.com/business/54348

slides.title: 优秀企业家的最高行为准则
slides.subtitle: Weiwen Han on LinkedIn
slides.description: 中国人常讲： 修身，齐家，治国，平天下，这同样可以作为优秀企业家的最高行为准则，而这也恰好契合了可持续发展和ESG的理念。 修身，代表着企业家顺应时势不断调整自身心态，拓宽视野，立足长远。在“新常态”下，单纯依靠短视的资源消耗、数量扩张和价格竞争的模式已经难以为继，必须要走长期可持续发展道路，把重点转移到品牌美誉度，产品和服务的质量，效率的提升，员工的满意度等等。 齐家，代表着对企业的治理，对应着ESG中的“Governance”。当前中国的民营企业中超过90%仍属于家族式经营，普遍遭遇家族企业的组织管理难题，包括第一代创始人与继承者的交接问题，家族成员与外聘职业经理人的矛盾问题，家长制高度集权的文化冲突问题等等。而成功的家族企业是如何做的呢？以具有170多年历史的家族企业Cofra为例，Cofra成立于1841年，以服装公司起步，并于1911年成立C&A。贝恩研究成果表明，Cofra家族企业基业长青的关键要素有三：其一，家族成员的高度参与需要辅以高度结构化的家族治理框架（如明确家族成员在家族办公室中的角色和职责）方是最为有效的；其二为了确保家族成员的有效参与，家族企业需要针对参与企业业务的家族成员设置严格的条件（为下一代选择并培养有能力的指引者）；其三，独立的投资部门（私募股权基金和房地产）在维持家族财富的同时多元化业务组合方面具有重要作用。 治国，代表着对企业的员工到客户、从供应商到股东、乃至更大范围内的生态圈的关注和推动，暗合了ESG中的“Social”。在贝恩的全球案例库中，英特尔在推动供应链和雇员ESG指标提升方面有着卓越的表现。针对供应链，英特尔提出了三大举措：其一，对供应商设定明确指标，涵盖劳工、健康与安全、环境标准等；其二，与供应商保持紧密互动，并参与监督供应商的整个生产流程；其三，对供应商定期进行审计，专门设立供应商回报卡，促进供应商进行不断升级。针对雇员，尤其是工厂劳工加班问题，英特尔不仅设立了明确的加班标准，同时也为供应商开发了加班管控系统，对每一天每一周的生产计划进行监控和分析，从而保证工时的合理分配，严格控制加班时间。 平天下，代表着企业家对生态环境的责任和担当，对应着ESG中的“Environment”。SEE阿拉善生态基金会就是中国企业家关注环境问题的先驱，是由中国近百名知名企业家发起成立的民间非赢利环境保护组织，致力于内蒙古阿拉善荒漠地区的生态改善，并推动中国企业家承担更多的环境责任和社会责任，同时也是贝恩的公益合作伙伴和资助对象。阿拉善的三百多名企业家会员不仅仅提供资金捐赠，而是以自身企业作为表率，率先执行“绿色企业”标准并发布绿色发展报告，同时在各自行业领域倡导“绿色企业”概念并成为行业的标杆，成功树立了中国企业家关注社会责任的榜样。

headline: Partner @ Bain & Company | Innovation, Product Management & Venture Building
about:
I’m the leader of the Americas Innovation & Business-Building team at Bain & Co., where I help teams create new ventures, products, and customer experiences. 

With over 20 years of experience in industries like Financial Services, Healthcare, and Payments, I specialize in helping organizations build modern, product-led organizations and develop scalable innovation engines. My expertise spans wealth management, insurance, banking, fintech, and healthcare payors with an increasing focus on leveraging GenAI to create breakthrough products and solutions.

Whether designing new products or transforming a legacy business, I’m passionate about leading and investing in high-performing teams that drive innovation and achieve unexpected results.

What I Do

I partner with organizations to:

▶️Build and launch new ventures and products that drive growth
▶️Help companies become more product-led and digitally driven
▶️Facilitate customer-centric innovation and transformation initiatives
▶️Develop scalable systems for continuous innovation at large organizations

With a background as an entrepreneur and angel investor, I bring a unique blend of strategic vision and hands-on execution. My work spans the U.S., EMEA, and Asia, helping companies turn their most ambitious ideas into reality.

I’m particularly focused on using data, creativity, and emerging technologies (like GenAI) to deliver products and solutions that meet customers where they are and anticipate where they’re going.

Prior Experience

Before joining Bain as an expert partner, I served as an Entrepreneur-in-Residence at a major U.S. investment firm and a leading consumer products company, where I helped establish repeatable innovation units and trained teams to build businesses from the ground up.

I’ve also been a serial entrepreneur, including co-founding a fintech startup in EMEA that became a launch partner for Apple Pay and Android Pay, as well as innovating in mobile-specific fraud detection for payments.

A Little About Me

➕MBA, Stanford Graduate School of Business
➕B.A. in Economics, Davidson College
➕Adept in Agile and Lean product development methods
➕Former strategy consultant, entrepreneur in residence, angel/VC investor, and startup advisor
➕I love coaching teams to push the boundaries of what’s possible and create real impact

If you’re interested in exploring new ventures, collaborative innovation, or just want to have a conversation about the future of business, reach out to me at dennis.jones@bain.com. Let’s see how we can create something incredible together.

headline: Bain
topSkills: Corporate Development • Management Consulting • Private Equity • Strategy
about:
Jed has been a leader in Bain’s Private Equity and Advanced Manufacturing & Services Practices since becoming a Partner of the Firm in 2005. He co-founded the Chicago Private Equity Practice in 2005 and managed it for many years. Jed led more than 300 diligence assignments and growth strategy, cost reduction and performance improvement engagements for PE owned portfolio companies.

Over the past 18 years Jed has led Bain’s relationships with sophisticated middle market private equity investors.  In addition to his client responsibilities at Bain, Jed led Bain’s recruiting efforts at the University of Chicago Booth School of Business for a decade, served on the Board of the graduate school’s Business Solutions Group for 15 years, and was recognized with the Angel Alumni Award for exceptional alumni engagement and contributions to Booth.

Jed began his management consulting career with Andersen Consulting in 1993 following graduation from Dartmouth and spent four years with the Firm in the Process and Strategy Group focused with industrial products clients on logistics and supply chains working from offices in Miami and Atlanta, with extended assignments in France and South Korea.

Jed's academic credentials include an MBA from University of Chicago Booth School of Business, and both an AB degree and a BS degree in Electrical Engineering from Dartmouth College.
